subject: Block Coding (Sequential Events)
arc_note: Grade 1 · Ontario Math C3 (Coding), SEQUENTIAL events only — one actor, order matters, ≤6 blocks, NO loops, NO concurrency, NO variables. Lane = a tiny block PROGRAM (ScratchJr/Scratch-style coloured blocks with short DECODABLE word labels + an icon, e.g. green 'start at 0', blue 'forward 2', blue 'back 1') that moves Bit along a NUMBER PATH 0–6 — a computational representation of a mathematical situation (counting / adding & subtracting within 10), which is exactly where Ontario C3 sits. The program runs top-to-bottom; the RESULT is the number Bit lands on. Arc covers BOTH C3.1 (write & run a sequence) and C3.2 (read, alter, predict, describe, debug): read→order-matters→build→forward&back→predict-then-run→change-one-block→debug→plan-and-code. Every sheet: I-do/we-do/you-do scaffold, a 'predict before you run' prompt (C4-L4), and the teacher answer key explains WHY the order works / what breaks if reordered (C2-L4). Each landing number / altered result / fix is MODELLED + asserted in solution.py (a tiny sequential interpreter). G1 uses real text labels (light decodable reading), unlike symbol-only K. Cite C3.1 + C3.2 verbatim from the Grade-1 cache.
